title: 5a-2: ParseContext + core-owned tree-sitter infrastructure
description:
## Parent

sutra/30 (PRD: core model redesign)

## What to build

Move tree-sitter parser creation and lifecycle into core-owned infrastructure. Introduce ParseContext struct that provides the parsed tree to adapters. Implement parser pooling (one parser per language, reused) and timeout enforcement.

Adapters gain a grammar() method and receive ParseContext instead of raw source strings. Core calls grammar(), creates/pools the parser, parses the source, passes ParseContext to adapter.parse().

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] ParseContext struct defined: source bytes, tree-sitter Tree reference, file_path
- [ ] Core parser pool: one tree-sitter Parser per language, reused across files
- [ ] Timeout enforcement: configurable parse timeout with sensible default
- [ ] LanguageAdapter trait updated: grammar() method added, parse() receives ParseContext
- [ ] RustAdapter and DartAdapter updated to use ParseContext (no longer create own parsers)
- [ ] Parser pooling test: same grammar reuses parser across multiple calls
- [ ] Timeout test: pathological input respects timeout
- [ ] Behavioral parity: same parse output as before

## Blocked by

- sutra/31 (LanguageAdapter trait + registry)"

messages.author: codex
messages.text:
Codex review: needs-attention.

1. [high] Timeout can erase existing index for a changed file. parse_single_file deletes the old DB row before parsing; if timeout hits, file_id=0 is returned and no replacement is written. This is a pre-existing pattern but timeout makes it more reachable.

2. [medium] set_language failure now panics via expect() instead of returning SutraError::Parse. Recoverable error turned into process crash.
